said of oneself or of people in general, not of two parties toward each other: be content with what there is, after <tawh>, with; with <lo>, be dissatisfied
<kilungkim>, be satisfied, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not be content with something, not agree to it

terms: please one another/satisfy oneself/be made content
definition: <lungkimsak>, please or satisfy, with the prefix <ki>: please each other, or make oneself content with something
be interested in something and eager to know about it, said of people in general with the prefix <ki>; {kilunglut mahmah} is there is great interest
<lungnemsak>, make gentle or lowly in heart, with the passive prefix <ki>: be brought low, where the English has in his humiliation
<ki> and <lungneu> written as one word: be discouraged; {kilungneu sak} is let oneself be discouraged
<lungneu>, be downhearted, with the prefix <ki> and the causative <sak>: let oneself feel small and discouraged

terms: be glad with one another/be on good terms
definition: <lungnop>, be glad at heart, with the prefix <ki>: people feel glad with one another; with <bawl> or <sak> it is make one another glad

terms: comfort oneself/set one's mind at ease
definition: <lungnuamsak>, make glad or at ease, with the reflexive prefix <ki>
found in {kilungsim neihna}, holding something in the heart against one another, where the English has malice
<lungso>, be hot in heart, with the reflexive prefix <ki>: work oneself into anger or worry; found in {kilungso tawmsak}, make oneself fret
<kilungso> fret, with the causative <sak>: make oneself angry or worried
form of <kilungtuak>, be of one mind, used before <lohna> and <na>: {kilungtuah lohna} is disagreement and {kilungtuah na} is unity
<lung>, mind, and <tuak>, agree, with the reciprocal prefix <ki>: be of the same mind with one another to do something, here to do wrong
{Lup}, lie down, with the prefix <ki>; {kilup khoppih} means be lain with, in the sense of sexual intercourse.
passive of <lup>, here lay down: of a thing, be laid or set in a place, as the pot of beer set at the gate at <Khuado>
<lut>, enter, with the prefix <ki>: people go in, a place is entered, or one joins and takes part in something
Passive of <lutpih>, bring in, with the prefix <ki>: be carried or brought into a place, said of goods taken into a town.

terms: be let in/be admitted/be welcomed in
definition: Passive of <lutsak>, let in, with the prefix <ki>: be allowed to enter or be received into a place.
<kilut>, enter or take part, and <thei>, can, written as one word: one can enter, entry is possible
The area round about a person or place; {kim-ah} or {kim-a} after a noun means around it, as in {khua kim}, the country round a town.
Placed after a noun or verb: all of them without exception, each one, or the action done in full.
The middle or half of something: {zan kim lai} is the middle of the night, {kim ciang} is halfway up, and {kim khat} is a part of or some of.
placed after a number, an amount or a clock time to show that it is an estimate, as {inn 200 kim}, about 200 houses; not the area around a place and not every
Said of a woman who has been put away by her husband; often listed beside <meigong>, widow.
Boast about oneself or about what is still to come; compare <kisialh>, boast.
Divorce, a spelling of <kimakna> with a long vowel; {kimaakna lai} is a certificate of divorce.
{Kim}, surroundings, with the place marker <ah>, placed after a noun: around it, on every side of it.
<kim> in its meaning of all or every, with the place marker <ah>, after a noun: in every one of them, as {pawlpi kimah}, in every church, not around one place
{Mai}, face, with the prefix <ki>, each other: written before <ngat>, turn toward, or <tuah>, meet, to say that two parties face each other.
written apart before <sak>: {kimai sak} is <kimaisak>, be forgiven or forgive one another, often after <mawh> or <mawhna>, sin; {kimai sakna} is forgiveness of each other

terms: be on familiar terms/feel at ease together
definition: <ki>, each other, and <maingap>, feel at ease, written as one word: be unshy and familiar with one another
the reciprocal <ki> with <maingap>, feel at ease, and the noun suffix <na>: being at ease with one another, a close and unshy relationship
{Maingat}, face, with the reciprocal prefix <ki>: face one another, said of the two cherubim on the ark.
<maiphut>, meet face to face, with the prefix <ki>, one another: of two vehicles, run into each other front to front
Passive of <maisak>, forgive, with the prefix <ki>; {mawhna kimaisak} means sins are forgiven, and with {khat leh khat} it means forgive one another.
{Kimaisak} with the linking suffix <in>: being forgiven or forgiving one another; in Romans 2.15 excusing one another.
{Kimaisak}, be forgiven, with the noun suffix <na>; {mawhna kimaisakna} is the forgiveness of sins.
{Kimaisak}, be forgiven, with the plural <te>: those who are forgiven.
<maitai>, cheerful, with the prefix <ki>: be bright and cheerful toward one another, or with {nang leh nang} keep oneself cheerful

terms: cheer oneself up/put on a cheerful face
definition: {Maitaisak}, make cheerful, with the reflexive prefix <ki>: make one’s own face bright, put on a smile.

terms: face each other/meet face to face/confront
definition: stand face to face with someone, as opponents in battle or in court

terms: facing each other/face to face/opposite each other
definition: {Kimaituah} with the linking suffix <in>: facing one another, face to face.
Passive of <maizumsak>, put to shame, with the prefix <ki>; with <lo>, not be put to shame.
{Makai}, lead, with the passive prefix <ki>: be led; {kimakai sak} means let oneself be led, and {kimakai khial sak} let oneself be led astray.
<makaih>, lead, with the prefix <ki>: be led, or lead and govern one another; {kimakaih zia} is the way of leading and <kimakaihna> is leadership
the way a people or group is led, <makaihna> with the prefix <ki>: leading and being led among themselves

terms: let oneself be led/be led by
definition: <kimakaih>, be led, and <sak>, cause or let, written as one word: let oneself be led or guided by someone or something
<kimakaih>, be led or lead one another, from <makaih>, lead, with <zia>, way: how a church, family, army or other group is led and run
{Makna}, divorce, with the prefix <ki>; {kimakna lai} is a certificate of divorce.
Passive of <mamsak>, straighten, with the prefix <ki>: be made straight.
Brought to an end, said of work, an offering or a period of time; {kiman khin} is completely finished.
Passive of <man>, catch: be caught, arrested or taken captive; {sal-in kiman} is be taken as a captive.
<manawh> with the prefix <ki>: people in general head toward something, things are moving in that direction; usually after <lam>
{Mancip}, seize and hold fast, with the prefix <ki>: be held captive; {a kimancip} before a noun means captive.
<kiman>, be arrested, and <ding> written as one word: will be arrested or held

terms: be of use/be used/be in effect
definition: Be of use or be in use; mostly negative, {bangmah-a kimang lo} is worthless, of no use; also last or stay in use for a time.
{Kimang}, be in use, with the linking suffix <in>; said of a gift that is in use only for a time.
<kimang> and <lo> written as one word: not stay in use, not last; {sauvei kimanglo} is not last long
A spelling of <kimangngilh>: be forgotten, said of past troubles that are no longer remembered.
Passive of <mangngilh>, forget, with the prefix <ki>: be forgotten; {kimangngilh bawl} is make oneself forget.

terms: make oneself forget/put out of mind/pretend to forget
definition: <kimangngilh> and <bawl>, make, written as one word: forget on purpose, put a thought aside or act as if one had forgotten
Be forgotten or passed over by chance; said of dead bodies left unburied because no one noticed them.

terms: be used straight on/continue in use
definition: <kimang>, be used, with <pah>, straight away; of the existing priests simply being kept in use
<kimang>, be used, with the causative <sak> and the plural <te>: people who are put to use by others
Passive with <ki> of <mangthangsak>, cause to perish: be destroyed, be cut off from one’s people.
{Kimang}, be of use, with <zaw>, more: be of more use, be better.
<kiman> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: a person was arrested or a thing was seized
{Kiman}, be caught, with the linking suffix <in> that joins it to the next verb: being caught, arrested or captured.
<kiman>, be caught, and the particle <kha> written as one word: get caught or arrested, also be caught in the hands when falling

terms: be arrested together/be seized along with
definition: <kiman>, be caught, and <khawm>, together, written as one word: be arrested together, or be seized along with a person
the passive <ki> with <mankhia> written as one word: be caught and taken out, said of arrested persons, of seized goods and of a captured animal

terms: be arrested at once/be caught right away
definition: <kimankhia>, be arrested, and <pah>, at once, written as one word
<kimankhia>, be caught, with the particle <ta>, now, already, written as one word: has now been caught; common in news reports before <cih> or <hi>

terms: be able to be caught/be successfully arrested
definition: <kimankhia>, be caught, and <zo>, manage to, written as one word; {kimankhiazo nailo} is has not yet been caught
<kiman>, be arrested, and <khin>, already, written as one word: have been arrested; in headlines after the number of people
<kiman.2> and <khinta> written as one word: have already been arrested
<kiman>, be caught, and <kik>, again or back, written as one word: be caught after running away, or be arrested in turn

terms: not be caught/not be arrested/not be seized
definition: <kiman>, be caught, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not be arrested, and of goods, not be seized
What something is good for; {a kimanna om lo} or {kimanna nei lo} means useless, worthless.

terms: be arrested at once/be caught immediately
definition: <kiman>, be arrested, with <pah>, at once, written as one word
<kiman>, be arrested, and <phot>, for the time being, written as one word: has been arrested or detained for now, while the case goes on

terms: let oneself be arrested/give oneself up/be caught
definition: the prefix <ki> with <mansak>, cause to seize, written as one word: let oneself be arrested, give oneself up; also be caught, of smuggled animals
{Kiman}, finished, with <siang>, clean: be wholly finished, said of work carried through to the end.
<kiman>, be arrested, with <suak>, right through: be arrested there and then, end up under arrest

terms: be arrested at once/be arrested on the spot
definition: <kimansuak>, be arrested, and <pah>, at once, written as one word
<kiman>, be arrested, with the particle <ta>, now, already, written as one word: has now been caught; common at the end of headlines
{Kiman}, be taken, with the plural <te>: those who have been captured; {sal-a kimante} are people taken captive, and after a battle the word also covers the plunder taken.

terms: can be caught/can be arrested/be caught
definition: <kiman>, be caught or arrested, and <thei>, able, written as one word: can be caught or arrested, was successfully caught; {kimanthei nailo} is has not yet been caught
<kiman> in the sense of cheap or good value, with <zaw>, more: costing less, or being more worth the cost
{Kiman}, be caught, with <zo>, be able or enough: said of fish, whether enough could be caught.
Be spared, be left alive; {na nuntakna hong kimap ding} means your life will be spared.
{Kima}, divorced, with the completive suffix <sa>: said of a woman who has been sent away by her husband.
<masak> with the prefix <ki>: be put first, be treated as coming before the others
Passive of <mat>, seize, with the prefix <ki>: be arrested, be caught or be taken captive.
Holding or sticking to each other; said of parts that are joined or fitted together.
<kimat>, be caught, and <kihen>, be bound: be arrested and held by the police or the immigration office; with <na> after it, an arrest or detention

<kimat>, be arrested, and <kihenna>, being bound or imprisoned, set side by side: arrest and detention by the police or immigration officers, said of refugees and migrants; one meets with it, {kimat kihenna tuak}

terms: be arrested in addition/be arrested as well
definition: <kimat>, be arrested, with the ending {-beh}, in addition, as in <behlap>: one more person is arrested besides those already held; in news reports usually followed by <leuleu>, again
{Kimat}, hold together, with <cip>, firmly: be stuck fast or tightly closed, said of a hand stuck to a sword, a sealed book and scales shut together.
{Theih}, know, with <ma>, before, and the prefix <ki>: be known beforehand; {a kimatheih lo} is something that cannot be known in advance.
{Kimat}, be joined, with the linking suffix <in>; after <tawh> it means next to or connected with.
<kimat>, be arrested, with the negative <loh> written as one word: not be arrested; {akimat leh kimatloh} is whether arrested or not
{Kimat}, be caught, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of being caught or taken.
{Kimat}, hold to each other, with the causative <sak>: join things so that they hold together, as curtains with clasps.
{Kimatsak}, join things so that they hold together, with the linking suffix <in>; said of foxes tied tail to tail.

passive of <mawhsak>, blame: a person or body is blamed by others for what was done, often as {kimawhsak mahmah}, is much blamed, while with {khat leh khat} the meaning is accuse one another
{Kimawhsak}, condemn oneself or accuse one another, with the linking suffix <in>.
An accusation made against someone; also the condemning of oneself in the heart, a guilty conscience.
{Kimawhsakna} with the plural <te>: the things a person is accused of.

the prefix <ki> joined to <mawk>, idly or for no reason, and written before the verb that <ki> belongs to: {kimawk tot}, quarrel for no reason; {kimawk hoho}, chat idly with one another; {kimawk phat}, praise oneself emptily
{Mawkphat}, praise idly or flatter, with the reflexive prefix <ki>: flatter oneself.
of a trap, spring shut with nothing in it

terms: quarrel without cause/accuse for no reason
definition: {Mawk}, idly or without reason, with <kitot>, quarrel: pick a quarrel with someone for no reason.
Play, as children do; also perform or hold a contest for others to watch
<kimawl> and <ding> written as one word: will play, those who are to play; {kimawlding hun} is the time of the games
<kimawl>, play, with the linking ending <in>: playing
<kimawl>, play, and <khawm>, together, written as one word
<kimawl>, play, with its last syllable repeated: play on and on or play about with something; with <a> or <khat> also the one who does so
<kimawl>, play, with the noun suffix <na>: a contest in which athletes compete

<kimawlna>, game, with the plural <te>
<kimawl>, play, and <ni>, day, written as one word: the day on which a game, match or show is held
<kimawl>, play, with the suffix <pih>: play together with someone, or play with something as a toy
<kimawlpih>, play with, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of playing with someone, also rough play with a person
<kimawl>, play or perform, with the causative <sak>: have someone perform or hold a contest before onlookers
<kimawl>, play, with <siam>, skilled: one who is good at sport or games
<kimawl>, play, and <siampen>, most skilled, written as one word: the best player of a competition
<kimawl> play, with the plural <te>: the ones who are playing, here of children
<mazang>, make progress, with the prefix <ki>: people get ahead and are effective in work or in life; paired in one article with <kilawhcing>, succeed
The halfway point of the height or extent of a thing; <kim>, middle, with <ciang>, as far as.

terms: each and every one/every one/all alike
definition: <kim> and <ciat> written as one word after a verb or noun: every one without exception, each of us; common in blessings, as {hong pia kimciat ta hen}, may he give to each one of us
Be squeezed or pressed flat, be crushed; passive with the prefix <ki>.
A spelling of <kimeltheih>: know one another by sight, be acquainted; <tawh> marks the other person.
Passive with <ki> of <meetsak>, have the wool cut off: be shorn.
the prefix <ki> and <meksak> written as one word: be squeezed or pressed with the hand, or be made to press; {gawl kimeksak} is be gripped by the throat
the prefix <ki> with <mel>, appearance, used before <theih> or <thei>: {kimel theih} is know one another, be acquainted, and {kimel theihna} is acquaintance
{Meltheih}, know by face, with the reciprocal prefix <ki>: know each other, be acquainted; <tawh> marks the other person.
<kimeltheih>, know each other, with the noun suffix <na>: the state of knowing one another

terms: be connected/have to do with each other
definition: of two things, belong together or rest on one another; here said of keeping the law and faith, with <lo>: have nothing to do with each other
<kimemat> be connected with, with the noun suffix <na>: something that ties a person to a matter and gives a right in it

<met.3>, profit, with the prefix <ki> for people in general: one gains by something, it pays; not the passive of <met.1>, shave; {kimet zaw} is it pays more
said of the age-old hills before God, in parallel with <kitamkham> crumble; how the word is built is not certain
Passive with <ki> of <met>, shave: of a beard, be shaved clean away.
Passive of <mettol> with the prefix <ki>: of the head, be shaved completely, as a sign of mourning.

terms: be shaved bald/have the head shaved
definition: <kimettol> be shaved bald, with <sak>: have the hair shaved off completely, as a sign of mourning
{Kim}, complete, with the suffix <in>: the whole of it, with nothing and no one left out; often as {a kimin}.
after a number, a year or a time of day: roughly that many or at about that time, not exactly; here <kim> is around, not complete

terms: be dishonoured/be disgraced/be put to shame
definition: Passive with <ki> of <mindaisak>, bring a name into disgrace.
Be given a bad name: <min>, name, with <sia>, bad, and the causative <sak>, passive with <ki>.
Passive of <minthangsak>, glorify; <minthang> is shortened to <minthan> before <sak>.
Passive of <minthangsak>, glorify, with the prefix <ki>: be glorified, be honoured.
Passive with <ki> of <min>, name, <than>, be renowned, and the causative <sak>: be made famous, be glorified.
{Kiminthansak}, be glorified, with the noun suffix <na>: that by which someone is glorified.
Passive of <mitsak>, put out, with the prefix <ki>: of a fire or of anger, be put out; mostly negative, {kimitsak lo ding hi}, it shall not go out.
{Mittaw}, blind, with the prefix <ki>, oneself, and the causative <sak>: make oneself blind.
An indefinite number or part of a group or thing, placed after the noun; repeated, some and others; of a divided thing it can be one half.
Some among a group, placed after the noun that names the group.
Some among a group, placed after the noun that names the group; also one half, as in {Manasseh minam kimkhatte}, the half-tribe of Manasseh.
A spelling of <kimkhatte> found once, at the start of a sentence: some among them.
Some of them, here some of the seed; apparently a misprint of <kimkhatte>.
On every side of a person or thing; written after a noun or after <a>, often with the endings <a> or <ah>.
used as a verb before <hi> or after <hong> and <na>: be all around someone or something, or move in a circle around it as the moon goes around the earth
{Kimkot}, around, with the ending <a> that links it to the following noun: that which is around.
{Kimkot}, around, with the place marker <ah>: on every side of the thing named before it.
{Kimkot}, around, with the suffix <in>; after a noun, going or lying all around it.
{Kimkot}, around, with <teng>, all: the whole surrounding of a thing, placed after the thing surrounded.
Placed after a descriptive word or clause: while still being so, even though it is so; often followed by {hi napi}, although.
<Kimlai>, while, with the intensive <pi>: at the very time that something is so.
<kimlai>, while, with <tak>, written as one word after a verb or a time word: just at the moment when it was so; {zan kimlaitak} is right at midnight
<kim>, <le> and <paam> written as one word: all that lies around, the surroundings; in the articles the natural environment
<kim>, <le> and <pam> written as one word: everything and everyone around one
<kim>, all or fully, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not all of them, not in every case; {ki kimlo} is not equal, not the same for everyone
with <lung>, heart: {lung kimlohna} is not being satisfied, displeasure, the noun of <lungkim> with <lo>
<kim> all, complete, with the noun suffix <na>, placed after a verb: the doing of it in full, to every one or in every detail; {tunpih kimna} is the bringing of all of them
after <thu>, word, a spaced spelling of <thukimna>: agreement between parties, not the doing of something in full; {thu kimna nei} is reach an agreement
{Kim}, around, with <nai>, near, and the place ending <a>; {a kimnai-a om} means which is close by.
<mot>, idly or senselessly, with the prefix <ki>, placed before a verb: the thing is done without thought or restraint
<kim>, surroundings, with <pawl>, written as one word after a time or year: around that time, about then
<kim>, about, and <pha>, reach, written as one word, placed after a number: the count or distance comes to about that many
apparently a misprint of <kumpipa>, the king
make the heart content: <kim>, complete, with the causative <sak>, used after <lung> or <lungsim>, heart, as in {ka lung hong kimsak}, it pleases me
of something sour acting on the teeth, as vinegar does
<kim>, all, complete, with <tak>: in full, with nothing and no one missing; often {kimtak in}
<kim>, complete, with <takin>, which makes an adverb: in full, with nothing lacking; usually written {a kimtakin}
<kim> with the plural <te>, placed after a noun; {minam kimte} is all nations
after a number, <kim> in the sense of about with the plural <te>: roughly that many persons or things, as in {galkap 100 kimte}, some 100 soldiers
<kim>, all, and <tek>, each, written as one word after a verb or noun: all of them, each one without exception
<kim>, surroundings, with <teng>, all of: the whole area around a place, often followed by <ah>
see each other, come together with someone: <mu>, see, with the reciprocal prefix <ki>; <tawh> marks the person met
passive of <mu>, see: a thing is seen or found, with no <tawh> and no person who is met; <kimuh> is the form before endings

<kimu>, see each other, and <tek>, each one: with <ni> after it, {kimu tek ni}, let us all see each other; a closing formula of a writer or broadcaster, see you all there, with the place of meeting before it
<muak>, go to meet or welcome, with the prefix <ki>: be welcomed; {hong kimuak hi} says that persons are welcome, and of a feast day, be celebrated
<ki> and <muam> written as one word: be kept in the mouth without being swallowed; {thu kimuam} seems to be a matter kept to oneself
what a person relies on; {ei leh ei kimuan'na} is trust in oneself

terms: be confident/rely on oneself/trust in oneself
definition: <muang> trust, with the reflexive prefix <ki>; {kimuang takin} is confidently
<muang>, trust, with <ki> as a passive: be trusted by others, mostly with <lo> of a person, a company or a government that people do not trust
reciprocal <ki> with <muangmawh> doubt, be unsure of

terms: have confidence in oneself/dare to trust oneself
definition: <kimuang>, trust in oneself, and <ngam>, dare, written as one word; follows {amah leh amah} or <ei le ei>, oneself, and is mostly used with <lo>, not
<muanlah>, doubt, with the prefix {ki-} and the noun suffix <na>: lack of trust in oneself or in one another
<kimuan> with <lohna>, not being: not trusting oneself, lack of confidence; between people, lack of trust in each other
<muanmawhna>, suspicion, with the reciprocal prefix <ki>: distrust of one another
<muanna>, trust, with the prefix <ki>: trust in oneself, confidence; {kimuanna lungsim} is a confident heart
the courage to rely on oneself, often after {amah leh amah}, and also trust that people dare to place in one another
passive of <mudah>, hate: be hated by others
with {khat leh khat}, hate each other; with <tawm>, loathe oneself
<kimudah> hate each other, with the linking ending <in>

terms: set at odds/cause to hate each other
definition: <kimudah> hate each other, with the causative <sak>
<kimudah> hate, with <tawm>, oneself, by oneself
<kimu>, meet, with <ding>, will, written as one word
passive form of <muh> see, used before endings such as <theih>, <leh> and <ciangin>
form of <kimu> used before endings such as <ciangin>

terms: be found in addition/be found as well
definition: passive <ki> with <muhbeh> written as one word: further ones are found besides those already found
<kimuh>, see each other, and <cil>, at first, written as one word: when people have just met for the first time
<kimuhcil>, be seen or met for the first time, with the noun suffix <na>: the time or place where something was first found, or the first meeting with someone
reciprocal <ki> with <muhdah> hate; {kimuhdah sak} is cause to hate each other, set at odds
<kimuhdah> with the noun suffix <na>: the state of being hated or unloved, and also hatred between people
<kimuh>, meet, with <ding>, written as one word: to meet, the meeting that is to take place; {tawh kimuhding} is to meet with
<kimuh> and <khawm> written as one word: meet with one another, come together, with <tawh> for the other party
<kimuh> and <khialhna> written as one word: people seeing one another wrongly, a mistaken view of each other; often beside <kitelkhialhna>
<kimuh>, meet, and <khop>, together, written as one word, the form used before <ding>, <hun> and {-na}: meet with one another; {kimuhkhop hunding} is the time set for a meeting
<kimuh>, see each other, and <khopna>, being together, written as one word: a meeting at which people or groups come together to see and talk with one another
<kimuh> and <kik> written as one word: meet one another again after being apart
<kimuh>, be seen, and <loh>, not, written as one word; {kimuhloh bawl} is act as if a thing were not seen
<kimuh>, meet, and <loh>, not, written as one word: not having met someone
with <bawl>, do: act as if one had not seen a wrong
<kimuh>, be found or be seen, with {-na}: the place, the person or the way in which something is found or seen
<kimu>, meet, with {-na}: a coming together of people to talk, after <tawh>, with, and with <nei>, hold; not the being found of the other sense
<kimuh>, meet, and <nading>, for, written as one word: for meeting each other, as the place where a meeting is to be held
<kimuh> meet, see each other, with <nop> wish; used with <tawh> for the person
<kimuh> meet, with <pih> together with; {na kimuhpih peuhpeuh}, anyone you meet
the prefix <ki> with <muhsak>, show, written as one word: be shown to others, or let oneself or one's work be seen
<kimuh>, see one another, with <sawm>, intend, written as one word: plan or try to meet each other

terms: be seen below/be looked down on
